text:
maria: quick heads-up — CI failing for sample-app when we publish the dual package build. edge sample (Vercel Edge) works in dev, but on CI the node sample throws: "Cannot use import statement outside a module" and our published tarball is missing d.ts files. anyone seen this? :confused:

jeff: ugh. most likely our package.json conditional exports aren't lined up with the tarball layout. do we have both dist/esm and dist/cjs in the package? also what does package.json look like (type/module/main/exports)?

maria: here's the relevant slice from the failing release candidate:```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/sdk",
  "version": "0.8.0-rc.3",
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "dist/esm/index.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "files": ["dist"]
}
```

talia: two quick notes: 1) for Vercel edge you must ship ESM entrypoints (they prefer import paths). 2) conditional exports are recommended to avoid consumers hitting the wrong field. e.g.```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.js"
  }
}
```
and keep a top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts". if types aren't in the tarball CI will fail type-import checks.

samir: also watch out: some packagers (npm pack) will drop files if "files" isn't set right or .npmignore blocks d.ts. we had a bug where tsconfig outDir was "lib" but files pointed to "dist" — mismatch in build step. add a smoke CI job that runs `npm pack` and inspects the tarball contents.

maria: good call. current CI shows the tarball doesn't contain dist/index.d.ts nor dist/esm/index.js (only dist/cjs). so the publish step is running `npm pack` against the wrong artefact (we build esm to a different folder in the mono repo pipeline).

jeff: another edge gotcha — when publishing dual packages, some consumers get `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` because they resolve to the import entry but try to require() it. conditional exports with import/require handles that, but you also need to keep a CJS build for legacy node. Node resolution looks at "exports" first, so make sure the paths exist in the package root.

talia: for typings: Node/NPM supports putting "types" inside exports too:```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  }
}
```but this is relatively new — bundlers and TS sometimes still prefer the top-level "types" field. safest is to keep both.

samir: sample-app bug was also reproducible when using an esbuild-based runner that treated the package as CJS unless package.json had "type":"module". but adding "type":"module" breaks CJS fallback for require() consumers. that's why conditional exports + dual bundles is the balanced approach.

build-bot: [automation] package validation failed on v0.8.0-rc.3: missing files: dist/index.d.ts, dist/esm/index.js. tarball inspected at 2024-04-24T12:03:11Z.

maria: proposed fixes: (1) unify build outputs to dist/esm and dist/cjs (2) add explicit "exports" with import/require/types keys (3) ensure "files" and .npmignore include d.ts (4) CI: add `npm pack` + quick require/import smoke test and inspect tarball for d.ts.

jeff: +1. I'll open a small PR that updates package.json and the publish job, and add the pack+inspect step as a separate pipeline stage.

talia: can we also add a tiny sample-app CI across node 18 (CJS), node 20 (ESM default), and a Vercel-edge-like esbuild runner so regressions show up fast?

samir: I'll add the smoke test and a script `scripts/ci-validate-package.sh` that unpacks the tarball and asserts presence of these paths. snippet:```bash
npm pack --silent
TAR=$(ls *.tgz | head -1)
mkdir -p /tmp/pkg && tar -xzf "$TAR" -C /tmp/pkg
jq -r '.[] | .path' /tmp/pkg/package/package.json || true
test -f /tmp/pkg/package/dist/index.d.ts
test -f /tmp/pkg/package/dist/esm/index.js
```

maria: perfecto. thanks y'all — main blocker is mismatch between build output paths and package.json exports. once the PR lands we'll re-run the failing sample-app CI. :thumbsup:

build-bot: [automation] created issue #1429: "packaged artefacts missing ESM/typing entries for @redwood/sdk" assigned to @jeff and @samir.
